title: How to search the CSSBuy spreadsheet and find older listings
summary: A product can sit hundreds of rows below the homepage and still have a live listing. Use the catalogue count, search scope and marketplace ID to find it again.

sections.heading: Read the range above the products
paragraphs: Open the full spreadsheet from the homepage. Look at the range beside the product count. The first number tells you where the visible selection begins, the second tells you where it ends, and the last is the number of listings in the current selection. That last qualification matters. A page of shoes and a page of search results each have their own total. To see the catalogue count, clear the search box and choose all categories. The handful of products featured on the homepage serves as a set of entrances into this larger collection.

During our November 28 check, the unfiltered catalogue contained 6,364 listings. The last four included two Pop Mart entries, a card bag and a cap. Finding a cap at the end of that list explains a common frustration: scrolling to the bottom of the homepage would never reveal it. Use the page selector on the full spreadsheet to move directly to the last page. As listings enter or leave the source catalogue, the displayed count and the products at either end can change. Bookmark the product when you find it.

sections.heading: Start with the most distinctive searchable word
paragraphs: Imagine trying to find a shoe you saw yesterday. You remember a lightweight runner with a sculpted sole, but the seller called it an XLG Runner Deluxe. Typing a whole sentence about the sole gives a text search many ways to miss. Start with XLG. Try the model name on its own, then add a category if the results still include unrelated goods. Preserve spaces and punctuation in your original notes so you can try a second spelling if a seller has written the letters together.

A category works well when you recognize an object but have little vocabulary for it. If you want a shoulder bag, begin with the accessories section and look for related seller words such as messenger, waist bag or crossbody. A seller may put more than one of those descriptions in a single title. Searching a translated phrase can help, although the public listing may still use English or a brand abbreviation. Try the model code as printed on the item before concluding a translated search has exhausted the possibilities.

sections.heading: Use each sort order for a different question
paragraphs: Use the latest order when you are looking for something that recently appeared. Change to popular when you want to see which listings draw attention in a category. Popularity tells you where other people have looked. It gives you no measurement of fit, build quality or current stock. A plain shirt near the bottom of the popularity list can suit your measurements better than a frequently opened one. Keep the feature you are looking for in view as you move through the results.

Price order is most informative after you have narrowed the product family. A shoe accessory can cost less than a pair of shoes and appear beside footwear in broad search results. Open each candidate, check what the seller includes, and use the same display currency for the comparison. Compare the price of the intended style and size at the destination. A catalogue thumbnail can illustrate a premium option even when the amount beside it is a listing-level price. For bundled goods, also check the unit and quantity before copying a figure into your notes.

sections.heading: Compare two listings without losing your place
paragraphs: Open each promising product in its own tab. Keep the original search results open with their query and sort settings. On a phone, the browser's open-in-new-tab gesture is especially helpful when a category contains many similarly named products. For each candidate, record its marketplace item ID, the distinguishing label or photo, and the option you would actually choose. Two rows with the same shoe name can lead to different sellers. Similar wording alone gives you no reason to merge them into one candidate.

Consider a rain jacket offered in black in two listings. One gallery shows the hood and the cuffs clearly. The other shows the lining and the inside label. That is enough to write two different follow-up questions while both pages are open. Check the hood adjustment on the second listing and the lining on the first. You have made more progress than you would by copying both prices and picking the lower one. Save the direct link beside each question so the seller's answer can be associated with the right garment.

sections.heading: Recover a product when the catalogue has moved
paragraphs: Listings can shift position when new entries arrive. If a saved page number opens to unfamiliar products, start with the marketplace link or a saved product page. Read the item ID from the detail view. A directory page may use a short internal number in its address while the seller uses a longer number for the original item. For example, the XLG Runner Deluxe listing has a catalogue path ending in 3470.html and displays marketplace ID 7876894732. Only the latter identifies that item on Weidian.

A screenshot of a results page is still useful if you lost the link. Crop the product card or retrieve the original image, open the camera beside the search box, and compare several candidates from the visual results. A close picture match can lead to the original listing even when its English title has changed. Check a second detail, such as the side panel or care label, before accepting the match. Where two sellers use the same image, the item ID can settle which listing you originally saved.

sections.heading: Keep a shortlist you can use at the buying page
paragraphs: For each finalist, record the item ID, seller link, pictured style, selected size and the time you last checked the price. Include one reason the listing is still on your list. A reasonable entry might say that the size chart includes the shoulder measurement you need or that the gallery shows the underside of a bag strap. Keep unanswered questions next to those facts. A blank field is easier to revisit than an assumption disguised as a measurement.

When you open the CSSBuy purchase link, compare the destination against your shortlist before entering a quantity. Check the ID, unit, colour, size and current amount in the same visit. If a different buying platform offers another view of the listing, the same checks apply there. This matters particularly when an external page chooses a default size on first load. A saved link is a way back to a product. The order screen records the option you are about to submit.

sections.heading: Diagnose an empty result in a few deliberate moves
paragraphs: Work outward from the last setting you changed. Clear a specific colour, remove a restrictive category, then search the core model again. Try the all-products view directly if the header shows a category total smaller than expected. If a visual search suggested an item, follow that result to its detail page before typing its translated title into a different search. Search words and pictures can lead to the same product by different routes, and each route preserves different clues.

If you still cannot locate the entry, note what remains observable. A working original seller URL establishes that the marketplace item exists at the moment you opened it. A matching catalogue row establishes directory coverage. A selectable option on the destination establishes what that page currently presents for purchase. These checks answer three different questions. Recording which one failed gives you something precise to revisit later, whether you are waiting for a catalogue refresh, an option to return, or clearer photographs.

title: CSSBuy image search: finding a listing from a product or style photo
summary: Start with one image, then test what makes the object distinctive. This guide follows a real screenshot through the search results and explains how to handle duplicates, close crops and missing matches.

sections.heading: Choose the photograph that answers your question
paragraphs: A photo search starts with a decision about the object you want to recognize. In a photograph of an outfit, the jacket may be prominent while the bag you actually want occupies a small corner. Crop around the bag, retaining its full outline and the way the handles attach. Search the whole outfit only if your question concerns the main item in the frame. A sensible crop removes competing objects while preserving information someone would use to tell two products apart.

For a shoe, a side view often preserves several features together: sole profile, number of eyelets, panel shapes and the position of a stripe. A close crop of a logo can lose most of those features. For a pair of jeans, the front view may tell you the cut while a rear pocket reveals an unusual stitching pattern. Save both images if you have them. They give you two independent ways to narrow a result set without guessing the exact words used by the seller.

sections.heading: Use the camera in the spreadsheet
paragraphs: Open the camera beside the search field or go directly to Image Search in the navigation. On a phone, choose a photo from your gallery. On desktop, you can choose a file, drop it into the search area, or paste a copied image. When pasting, copy the picture itself. Copying the page address puts text on the clipboard, which serves a different purpose. The interface accepts JPG, PNG, WebP and GIF images up to the stated size limit.

Wait for the catalogue progress indicator to finish before judging the result. The matcher compares the submitted picture with an index in the browser. Downloading the searchable data and comparing the images are separate from identifying an item. If the progress count is still moving, a slow connection may simply be loading the index. Keep the tab open. If the site specifically reports that loading failed, use the retry control once the connection is available again. A readable photo and a completely loaded index give the search its best starting point.

sections.heading: Read the first results as a shortlist
paragraphs: In our preview test, we cropped the homepage picture of a pair of Balmain/Purple/Amiri jeans and pasted it into Image Search. The original catalogue listing appeared fourth. Similar jeans occupied earlier positions. That ordering is instructive: a tight crop changes the amount of background and fabric visible, while several sellers may photograph dark denim against nearly identical backgrounds. Even when the original listing is present, the highest-ranked photograph can belong to another product with a similar composition.

Read several results before you follow a purchase link. Open a plausible candidate and look for two details that occur together in your reference. On jeans this could be the wash pattern across the thigh and the shape of the rear pocket. On a jacket it might be the pocket flap and how the zip meets the collar. If both details line up, move on to its style selector. If one detail plainly conflicts, return to the next candidate even when the first picture initially felt convincing.

sections.heading: Locate the matched photo within the listing
paragraphs: A seller may use a collage on the cover and individual views in the gallery. The image you searched can correspond to a small style thumbnail halfway down the product page. Look at the selected image, open the other views, and compare the style labels. A gallery match establishes that the image is associated with the listing. You may still need to pick the pictured colour and a size before the buying page can identify a particular SKU.

Pay attention to which image group you are viewing. The product gallery describes the listing. The style section presents selectable appearances where the source supplies them. Explicitly identified QC images serve a separate purpose and appear below the buying controls. A background with a ruler or a warehouse-looking floor does not by itself establish that a picture documents your order. After ordering, use the order-specific photographs in your agent account to review the unit received for you.

sections.heading: Try a second crop when several results look alike
paragraphs: Make one meaningful change to the input at a time. If your first crop includes a seller banner, remove the banner and keep the item at about the same scale. If the first crop shows only a toe box, include the heel and the sole. Compare the result sets and look for candidates that survive both attempts. This small experiment is more informative than repeatedly searching the same picture after changing its file name, which leaves the visible content unchanged.

Where the input is a four-panel collage, search one clean panel, then a different panel of the same option. Keep enough context to distinguish the orientation. One panel of a bag might show its front clasp, another its detachable strap. A candidate that agrees with both is worth a closer look. If two listings both pass, write down their item IDs. Sellers can reuse images and product names. At that point the search has narrowed a visual question as far as the photos allow, and the listing details must resolve the rest.

sections.heading: Understand image coverage and catalogue updates
paragraphs: The checked index covers 178,215 images associated with 6,364 catalogue products. It includes product pictures, seller-gallery images and style images. Those figures describe the indexed snapshot. The catalogue fetches current listing pages separately, so a recently changed thumbnail can appear on a live detail page before its new image enters the search index. A missing match is plausible even when you can reach the product by text search and browse its pictures manually.

For an item you found through a friend, ask for the original image or marketplace item ID. An image forwarded through several messaging apps may have a new border, heavy compression or a cut-off edge. A clean crop can still be useful, but an item ID gives you a direct way to compare the listing. If the gallery now shows different pictures, save the updated listing and compare the candidate manually. Repeatedly uploading the older file cannot add a missing new photo to an existing index.

sections.heading: Finish with a check another person could repeat
paragraphs: Before sharing a result, put the input and candidate side by side. Write a short observation such as “the seam passes below the left pocket and the button has a double rim.” That is more helpful than saying the pictures look identical. Include the marketplace item ID and a clear style label. Someone with the link can then open the relevant listing, choose the option, and check the same features without having to recreate your crop or search ranking.

If your goal is a purchase, repeat the colour and size check on the destination. Where the gallery has no measurement for the detail you care about, record the missing measurement in your order notes or ask the relevant seller or agent before committing. Image search does its job when it reduces a large catalogue to a few listings you can inspect. Choosing among those listings still depends on the option, the available evidence and the current seller information attached to each item.
A practical way to preserve that comparison is to save the original product picture and one clean second view beside the URL. Record the date and the selected style in plain text. A search-result position can change when photos are added or when a different crop is used, so a direction such as “open the fourth result” can become ambiguous. The saved listing and its visual detail give a friend a much more reliable way to reproduce your choice.

title: How to choose a Weidian style and copy its SKU link for CSSBuy
summary: Follow one shoe from its catalogue listing through colour and size selection. Learn which number identifies the listing, when a style link is available and what to check if the buying agent opens a default option.

sections.heading: Identify the seller item before choosing a style
paragraphs: A Weidian listing can contain many purchase options in one place. Every shopper viewing the listing may see the same title and item ID while choosing a different colour, size or bundle. Start by finding the marketplace item ID beside the product title. Save that number with the seller link. If two tabs have different item IDs, they refer to different listings even when the first photo and the translated product names look very similar.

The Adidas XLG Runner Deluxe example makes the distinction concrete. Its catalogue address ends with 3470.html, while the product identifies the seller item as 7876894732. The shorter number belongs to the catalogue page. The longer one appears in the original Weidian address. Use the marketplace number when comparing destinations or asking an agent about the item. The number belonging to a particular sellable combination, known as its SKU, is a further identifier. It only becomes meaningful alongside the options that produced it.

sections.heading: Match the desired appearance in the style grid
paragraphs: Begin with the picture that made you save the listing. Open the scrollable styles section and look through the complete set of thumbnails. A numbered tile such as 01 may be the seller's own colour label. Another seller can assign the same number to a completely different shoe. Choose the thumbnail on the listing you actually intend to buy, then look at the enlarged image. Check a detail that separates neighbouring colourways, such as the heel overlay, outsole edge or lining.

In our review, the example shoe showed 22 pictured options and 14 displayed sizes. That describes the page we checked and gives a good reason to scroll the options box before deciding. It does not tell you that every combination is still available today. Select the appearance first. If the image grid includes several very similar choices, capture the selected tile or note its exact wording before moving on. A note saying “01 on item 7876894732” is easier for someone else to verify than “the grey one.”

sections.heading: Choose a size and confirm the complete combination
paragraphs: A pictured style can have several sizes sharing one thumbnail. Select the needed size after the style and read both selected labels together. In the example, the 01 style and size 42 produced a combination for which the interface enabled the style-specific copy action. The number 42 here records the visible option. It does not establish that another brand or seller uses the same measurements. Consult the listing's own size information when fit is part of your decision.

If you change the style after selecting a size, inspect the size again. Some sellers offer different size ranges for different colours or package types. A prior size choice may cease to be valid. For products with additional option groups, finish those groups too. A set number, cable type or quantity can be as important as a colour label. Where several combinations could still fit the choices on screen, there is no reliable unique variant to copy. Recheck the selected fields and use the listing link with written instructions if a precise variant remains unavailable.

sections.heading: Choose the right link to send
paragraphs: Use the general Weidian link when sharing the whole listing so someone can choose their own size. Use the style-link control after you have selected the exact combination you want another person to review. The copied address carries the listing identification and, where the source provides it, the selected variant. Two addresses that begin with the same item ID can therefore communicate different choices. Keep the full copied text intact, including any portion after a hash mark, when pasting it into a note or message.

Test the handoff before you need it. Open the destination, compare the item ID, and read the colour and size it shows. Some apps display or preserve the original seller selection differently when opening a shared link. Give the recipient the literal style label and size as well as the URL. That small addition lets them recover the choice if their app opens the general listing. If the copy control displays a selectable address because clipboard access was denied, use the browser's normal copy command on that address.

sections.heading: Compare CSSBuy and other buying-agent destinations
paragraphs: The main purchase button opens the corresponding CSSBuy item. The other-agent panel lists available purchase destinations for the same marketplace listing. These links can represent the original item in different URL formats, and their visible page titles may be translated differently. Check the item ID where it is shown and compare the seller options on the destination you opened. If the agent opens a product preview with no size selected, choose the seller's matching style and size again before moving forward.

For a side-by-side comparison, hold the underlying selection constant. If one agent is showing a single shoe accessory and the other is showing a boxed pair, the prices do not represent the same choice. Read the unit, quantity and any packaging selection. Then put both figures into the same display currency and note the time you checked. The catalogue's currency switcher is useful for reading amounts, while the destination identifies the amount and options it currently presents for that purchase.

sections.heading: Interpret missing options and QC photographs
paragraphs: Sometimes the original seller page supplies one cover picture and no verifiable variant table. In that case the cover is still useful for finding the product, but it cannot identify a missing SKU. A long seller title mentioning many styles gives no dependable mapping from picture number to stock code. Use the seller page to look for the option information. If the data remains unavailable, keep the original listing link and request clarification with the picture and desired measurements attached.

The same discipline helps with photographs lower down the page. On the shoe used in our review, the detail view displayed four ordinary product images and zero pictures explicitly marked as QC. That is a meaningful observation. It tells you which visual questions you can answer from that particular listing. If you need to see the tag, sole length or condition of the pair received for you, use the inspection stage of your CSSBuy order. General gallery views can help you describe what you want checked when the parcel reaches the warehouse.

sections.heading: Write an order note that survives a translation change
paragraphs: Keep a compact record of the choice beside the URL. For the example the note might read “Item 7876894732, style 01, size 42. Please check the label against the selected size.” Add a distinguishing visual detail if the seller uses similar numbers or shorthand. Write the note after choosing the combination and before closing the page. If the next person uses a different site language, the seller's item number, style code and size can still be compared directly.

When two options look equally plausible, document the uncertainty and ask one question that would resolve it. For instance, request confirmation of whether the image shows the light lining or the dark lining for the selected option. This gives the recipient a precise reference to check. Once the question is resolved, reopen the destination and verify what is selected there. Only then does your record bring together the seller item, the intended SKU, the visual evidence and the choice that the buying agent will receive.

For repeat orders, reopen the saved item and run the same check again. A seller can revise a title, replace a photo or withdraw a size while keeping the listing address. Record the new selection only after it matches your earlier note. This is particularly useful for numbered colourways, where the text by itself offers very little help if the picture has changed.
